structuralFindings: Formal already encodes overheat as hard channel eligibility through lateStage; B has an additional ret20<=30 condition.
The 30<ret20<=35 and maDistance20Pct<=25 region is structurally A-eligible on notLate but B-ineligible on notLateB.
Research overheat starts earlier than Formal hard rejection (ret20>20, MA20 distance>12) and adds ATR/gap dimensions not present in lateStage.
Therefore overheatPenaltyResearch is not mechanically identical to lateStage, but both share ret20 and MA20-distance information.
A new generic Extreme Absolute Strength factor based mainly on the same return/distance/volatility dimensions would have high redundancy and is not justified as an additional score.
The useful open question is the protection/opportunity cost of the existing hard boundaries and the incremental value of the continuous research gradient inside the admitted region.

preregisteredQuestions: Within currently admitted A/B candidates, does continuous overheatPenaltyResearch add D1/D3/D5/MFE/MAE/stop/no-follow-through information after setupQuality, ATR, Residual RS, sector/regime and PV controls?
For B-like setups just above ret20=30 but below lateStage ret20=35, does exclusion protect downside/path quality enough to justify opportunity cost?
For A/B setups near MA20-distance 25, is hard rejection protective after ATR/liquidity/regime controls?
Are ret20 and MA-distance contributions redundant once ATR/gap/setup lifecycle are controlled?
Does effect survive crisis-date removal and independent scan dates?
falsification: If overheatPenaltyResearch loses incremental value after ret20/MA-distance/ATR/gap primitives and existing setup state, reject it as a derived research score rather than adding it to Formal.
If B ret20 30-35 rejects have worse downside/no-follow-through than matched admitted B setups, retain the B-specific bound.
If excluded boundary-near setups show stable OOS upside without worse MAE/cost/false-break and current boundary materially raises zero-pick, only then surface a boundary-reformulation candidate.
Do not search alternative 28/32/33/34/36 thresholds after outcomes.
Do not create a fourth Extreme Strength factor from the same primitives.
